events.summary:
This month we're building something real, live, for a real person.

THE BRIEF: A local bilingual early-childhood teacher wants to turn years of classroom
experience into printable Spanish/English curricula for children ages 1-5: weekly and
monthly plans, plus ready-to-print activities for math, language, art, sensory play and
motor skills. Teachers, childcare centers and families buy a download, print it and use
it the same day. The plan: sell on Teachers Pay Teachers and Etsy, promote on Pinterest, and let AI
help with ideas, organization and promotion without losing the teacher's own voice.

TONIGHT WE BUILD IT TOGETHER WITH CLAUDE CODE, starting from the teacher's written brief:

- A draft generator: pick an age, theme, skill and language, and get a weekly plan with
  learning objectives and matching activities, in both Spanish and English
- The teacher's voice, not the model's: a style guide and real examples so drafts sound
  like the teacher, with the teacher reviewing and approving every piece
- Print-ready output: a cover, instructions, the weekly plan and activity pages as
  letter-size PDFs
- Quality checks: age-appropriateness, bilingual accuracy, originality, and images that
  are safe to sell
- Selling without sending files: automatic delivery on the marketplaces, plus draft
  listings, preview images and Pinterest pins

WHY COME IF YOU'RE NOT A TEACHER? The pattern is the same one behind most useful AI
products: AI drafts, a human approves, and the system packages and delivers. You'll see
how to scope it, where AI helps, where it needs a human, and what it takes to make the
output good enough to sell.

Bring a laptop to build along, or just bring questions. Beginners and veterans welcome.
Hablantes de espanol bienvenidos.

EVENT DETAILS
Food, drinks and conversation from 7:00. Short show & tell at 7:20. Live build from 7:30.
Free to attend. Free parking at Gladstone Park SDA Church.
events.title: Build Night: From a Teacher's Idea to an AI-Powered Printable Business — Full Stack Devs PDX

The next in a regular series of local meetups for people who use the Fediverse or are interested in doing so!

About the Fediverse

Most social sites — such as X/Twitter or Instagram — are centralized and corporate owned. The Fediverse is decentralized and huge. FediDB currently tracks over 42,000 servers, run by thousands of independent operators. https://fedidb.com/servers

The Fediverse is not owned by a single company. It's an open, federated network of services on the Internet that speak a common communication standard.

There are many services on the Fediverse, such as social messaging, photo sharing, and video sharing. The Mastodon service is most popular for social messaging and chat. If you'd like to join the Fediverse, look into getting onto Mastodon. https://joinmastodon.org/

#### Topic

This talk explores why English captions alone may not provide meaningful access for many Deaf people, and how to build ASL access into digital experiences from the start. Shannon Eagen will walk through an online form example and a case study of a survey that places ASL videos alongside its questions and answer choices, then share practical design approaches.

Questions for the presenter may be submitted via chat during the meeting. They will be answered in writing after the presentation, and provided as a follow-up to attendees along with the presentation slides and a resource page.

#### Agenda

The event begins at 6:00pm; join early, starting at 5:45pm for networking.

* 5:45pm Networking
* 6:00pm Introductions and announcements
* 6:15pm Presentation
* 7:00pm Conclusion

#### About the presenter

Shannon Eagen is an accessibility advocate, Deaf education teacher, and Deaf Cultural and Linguistic Expert based in Vancouver, Washington.  She works across the Vancouver–Portland area and is active in the interpreting profession through RID, WSRID, and ORID. Her work and advocacy focus on language access, Deaf culture, and ensuring Deaf people can participate in services and communities in languages they understand.

#### RSVP

Please RSVP for the Zoom link: 

* [Meetup](https://www.meetup.com/portland-accessibility-and-user-experience-meetup/events/317413727/)
* [Eventbrite](https://www.eventbrite.com/e/captions-are-still-english-what-your-product-gets-wrong-about-deaf-access-tickets-2004823697648)
* [email](mailto:info@pdxa11yux.org)

#### Accommodation requests

If you have any accommodation requests, don't hesitate to get in touch with us before the event to discuss.

events.summary:
Summary:

Clear Linux OS is dead. For a lot of people who knew what Clear Linux OS was, that is sad. For a few people who worked on it, it's a giant loss of everything that we built, and everything we accomplished. Most of it was never made public - all the secret sauce.

I'm going to present why this was such a loss for everyone, and not just the users. The main thought is that we didn't just start a cool Linux distro. Because what we had to do was to appease the corporate lawyers, the Security guys, the product guys, and the management of the company, that doing Clear Linux OS was not a risk. And that it was a good idea to begin with.

And this means specifically that Compliance was important. And that we had a well oiled machine to keep producing updates, securely, and deliver speed and excellence to our users. And we did so - twice a day - for almost a decade.

This talk is going to be specifically about what I'm doing today to build a new OSS Linux Distribution factory. A machine that builds the distribution, that does all these things. And it does it with compliance at heart. And I'll tell you why I'm doing it like this. So that you can understand what is going to come out of it in the future, and what the value of that will be.

Follow the project at https://ur.foo-projects.org/ and come listen to my talk!

Bio:

Auke (pronunciation provided on request) Kok is a Dutch person living in Oregon since 2005, when he decided to quit a perfectly good job and move there, assuming it would be a good place to work on Linux stuff (and get paid). Before that period, he already studied CS in Amsterdam under Andrew Tanenbaum of Minix fame, and was a project lead for a Source-Based Linux Distribution. After the move to Oregon he worked for Intel for 17 years doing a little kernel work, and a lot of Linux Distribution Engineering. Auke founded the Clear Linux project with a few others, and built the distribution from scratch, and it was pretty neat. Nowadays he's no longer at Intel, and has figured out that Linux Kernel work isn't what he likes to do. So he decided to start a new Linux Distro project again, but this time, it's serious. Aside being obsessed about Linux Distributions and how they should work, Auke tries to stay in shape by rock climbing, and taking care of his own little piece of Oregon Forest up somewhere in the hills, together with his wife and three kids. To keep the house heated, he provides his experience and skills to Verge.IO where he is building the future Linux OS product that this company will offer as a product for those that wish to move away from VMWare and hosting their own private Cloud Infrastructure. Auke's blog posts can be found at ur.foo-projects.org.
events.title: Portland Linux/Unix Group General Monthly Meeting: a new OSS Linux Distribution factory, with Auke Kok

Fly Chai allow us to informally and freely use their space. If within your budget, we'd appreciate your help to sustain our use of the venue, by purchasing something tasty, whether Chai or otherwise.

Find us at tables with a Code&Coffee sign - or a clump of laptop-users!

Wifi and power outlets are available.
Our meeting area should be accessible - please let us know if not.

---- What to expect ----

Smaller events than you may be used to, with a mixed crowd week-to-week. We expect this is likely due to us meeting weekly, at a less central location.

These may result in what you're looking for:
    A smaller, less intimidating, lower pressure, cozy atmosphere.
    A mix of regular and new faces.
    A simpler schedule - every week, same time, same place - that you can drop into when you like.
    Being closer to you than other events.

Whether those are generally or partly to your liking, we hope you'll consider dropping by sometime!

---- Getting to the venue ----

Look for the venue on the meetup Google map, or alternatives like OpenStreetMap.

-- Driving --

There are limited parking spaces on a lot outside the venue (4+1 accessible), with more in the surrounding area.

-- Transit options --

Beaverton Central (Red/Blue MAX), then walk~ 8 minutes

Beaverton Transit Center (Red/Blue MAX, bus, WES) then walk ~11 minutes

For a shorter walk to the venue, take a bus from Beaverton Transit Center (52 to Farmington/Hall, 76 to Watson/Broadway, 57 to Canyon/Watson)
